maternal hypothyroid in late gestation alters Camk4 expression and Nurr1 labeling in the neocortical SP, a transient neuronal population that regulates neocortical connectivity.
maternal hypothyroid in late gestation delays the extinction of Camk4 expression and the maturation of SP in the neocortex.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of thyroid hormone in the development of the subplate and layer VIb in preterm children.
the role of maternal TH in the development of cortical SP cells.
the role of maternal hypothyroid state in the development of the cortical SP and layer VIb, two important areas of the cerebral cortex involved in the regulation of cognitive functions.

the expression of CamK4 in the cortical subplate neurons is delayed by late maternal hypothyroid state, and that this effect is more prominent in the subplate neurons compared with other cortical neurons, such as those in layer VI.

maternal THs regulate the timing of Camk4 extinction in the SP, which is a marker of cortical development and maturation.

thyroid hormones play a role in the development of the cortical subplate and layer VIb.
